questions.question: Describe how the team sets up and cooks the food item by following its flow chart, including the hygiene arrangements, the three readiness tests and the portioning.
questions.expected_answer: Before lighting the burner the chart is propped in view, a hand washing station with bucket, jug, soap and towel is set up if there is no tap, ingredients and equipment are laid out in order of use, and raw and ready boards are separated and labelled; everyone washes hands and the hygiene lead ticks the box. The pap cook sets water to boil first while the relish cook chops onions on the raw board. The oil is heated on medium, the onions fried and at five minutes tested by pressing against the pot, continuing if soft or frying two more minutes if firm; the tomato tin is opened only now, lid lifted by its edge, added and simmered two minutes; the pilchards are added gently with their sauce and broken into chunks; salt and curry powder are added and the sauce simmered ten minutes with the handle turned away. The pap meal is stirred smooth into the boiling water, covered on low heat for twenty minutes, with a portion thinned with milk powder and oil for the soft-food plates. At ten minutes the relish is tasted once with a clean spoon and adjusted if flat, then checked steaming hot and served, after hands are washed again, at about 250 grams of pap and 150 grams of relish per plate with soft portions kept separate; pots are lifted with a dry cloth, burners turned off and actual times written beside the planned ones.

questions.question: Explain how the cooked item is evaluated fairly for flavour and texture using agreed criteria and levels, and how its nutritional value is assessed.
questions.expected_answer: Tasters from another team, two or three per dish with a clean spoon each and water, use a sheet with the three criteria and four levels agreed before cooking, excellent, good, adequate and poor, each with a description so tasters agree, while the cooks listen and record without comment. Flavour asks whether the dish is seasoned so salt is not tasted as salt and spice is a warmth, the tomato and onion have cooked into the fish and a person would want more: excellent well seasoned and appetising, good pleasant but slightly under or over seasoned, adequate edible but bland or harsh, poor unpleasant or unsafe. Texture asks for soft onions, fish in chunks not mush, sauce thick enough to sit on pap, stiff smooth pap for adults and a smooth, thin, lump-free soft portion for children and the elderly, each on its own line. Nutritional value is reasoned, not tasted: the plate carries staple, protein, fat and vegetable, pap, pilchards, oil, tomato and onion; the portion of about 250 grams of pap and 150 grams of relish gives roughly 620 to 650 kilocalories against a 700 target, so a spoon of oil or bread is suggested; and fortified meal and the enriched soft portion are checked. Tasters score, write a sentence of evidence and sign.

questions.question: Set out the six parts of the written evaluation with examples, explain why specificity matters, and describe how the session is finished.
questions.expected_answer: One: what was made, for whom and against which brief. Two: results, the tasters' scores with evidence, actual times against planned, portions achieved and whether the specification of a nutritious, tasty, camp-cookable meal of 150 grams of relish served hot within two hours was met. Three: what went well with reasons, such as the relish ready in twenty-eight minutes because onions were chopped while water boiled. Four: what went wrong with causes, such as lumpy pap because meal was added too fast without stirring to a paste. Five: fixes made and improvements tied to causes, such as adding meal through the fingers while stirring, a spoon of oil to reach 700 kilocalories, tasting at eight minutes to leave time to adjust. Six: what it taught about camp cooking, that fuel and time are the limits, hygiene must be built into the sequence, the soft-food group needs its own portion. Specific statements earn marks and improve the next meal, so a diagnosed adequate outscores an unexplained excellent. The session ends with pots washed in hot soapy water, boards scrubbed, surfaces wiped, leftovers covered and eaten within two hours or discarded since there is no fridge, the last box ticked, and the chart with actual times, the signed tasting sheets and the evaluation filed in the design folder.
